name: Palace Hotel Tokyo
positioning: Contemporary luxury hotel in Marunouchi with a moat-side setting opposite the Imperial Palace gardens
best_for: Travelers who want a central Tokyo base beside the Imperial Palace gardens
Food lovers who want French, kaiseki, tempura and Chinese dining under one roof
Guests who want a full spa with pool and saunas

facts.text: The hotel has a moat-side setting just opposite the Imperial Palace gardens.
The hotel takes its name from being the closest hotel to the Imperial Palace.
In the early 2010s the hotel demolished its original early-1960s building and rebuilt it as a new luxury hotel.
Room interiors use leafy carpet motifs and earthy color palettes inspired by the nearby Imperial Palace gardens.
Rooms have open-style bathrooms with separate tubs and showers and bath amenities by Bamford.
Wadakura serves kaiseki, a refined style of Japanese dining.
Amber Palace serves Shanghainese and Cantonese cuisine, from Peking duck to dim sum.
The Palace Lounge is an afternoon tea setting by day and a cocktail lounge by night, with live jazz nightly.
In-room dining is available 24 hours a day for in-house guests.
The spa has heated baths, a marble sauna, a cold plunge pool, a dry sauna and separate men's and women's relaxation lounges.
In-house guests have access to an indoor swimming pool and fitness center.
Complimentary morning yoga sessions are offered to in-house guests on Saturdays and Sundays at the spa.

highlights.text: Esterre is a fine dining restaurant serving contemporary French haute cuisine in partnership with DUCASSE Paris.
Tatsumi is an intimate six-seat tempura bar.
The evian SPA design reflects the journey of evian water through the Alps, and each treatment room is named after an Alpine peak.
On a clear day, Mt. Fuji can be seen in the distance from the spa.
The Club Lounge, on the southeast corner of the 19th floor, is available to suite and Club guests.

considerations.text: The hotel is in the Marunouchi business district, which Conde Nast Traveler says has very little neighborhood flair.
Conde Nast Traveler's reviewer found that sometimes a little more English was needed from staff.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing that reflects the luxury positioning.
